official_measurement_examples.name: New marine-work permission service
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO's current get-permission service was published 18 November 2025 and separates marine licence, exemption and other-authority permissions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Marine licensing jurisdiction
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO is responsible for marine licensing in English inshore and offshore waters and licensing can extend into tidal rivers and estuaries.

official_measurement_examples.name: 13-week licence aim
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO says it aims to decide most marine licence applications within 13 weeks after validation, while individual cases can take more or less time.

official_measurement_examples.name: Maintenance dredging thresholds
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO dredging guidance distinguishes less than 500 cubic metres, 500 to 1500 cubic metres and more than 1500 cubic metres for possible exemption, accelerated or standard licensing routes, subject to conditions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Marine licensing fee regime
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO's marine licensing fee schedule current in 2026 includes application, monitoring and disposal-related charging structures.

official_measurement_examples.name: Harbour-order consultation register
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO's harbour-order register says applications appear when the statutory 42-day consultation starts or the mandatory EIA pre-application process for proposed works orders is completed.

official_measurement_examples.name: Harbour prioritisation framework
official_measurement_examples.fact: The February 2026 harbour-order framework can prioritise processing of qualifying applications but does not itself grant an order.

official_measurement_examples.name: Poole HRO current case
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO approved the Poole Harbour Revision Order 2026 on 30 June 2026 and the page states it came into force on 23 July 2026.
